sections.html:
A quick West Allis sale starts with a decision about the buyer: someone using a mortgage, someone you find yourself, or a buyer paying cash. Each one meets the same three Wisconsin requirements. The buyer receives a condition report, the state receives an electronic transfer return, and the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds records the deed. Taking a mortgage out of the picture drops the loan and appraisal steps, which is where most listings lose weeks.

West Allis sits in Milwaukee County. The 2025 population estimate is 60,119, a touch under the 60,325 counted in 2020, across 11.38 square miles of land.

The city is dense, with modestly priced homes and a lot of renters. Just over half of homes, 55.5 percent, are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $203,800. Your house competes with plenty of rental stock, so condition and presentation carry weight.

The 2020 census counted 29,015 housing units, 5.2 percent of them vacant. Interstates 94 and 41/894 cross the city, so commute questions are common. Planning a December listing? Candy Cane Lane, on Oklahoma and Montana Avenues between 92nd and 96th Streets, draws heavy traffic on holiday nights, which can complicate showings on those blocks.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin law asks of you
sections.html:
A seller of a building with up to four units owes the buyer a finished real estate condition report, delivered inside 10 days of the contract being accepted. Chapter 709 lets a buyer who gets nothing back out during the next two business days and recover deposits. Fiduciaries who never lived in the home, including personal representatives, trustees and conservators, are excused. So are transfers exempt from the transfer fee.

The state also charges the grantor a transfer fee, set by s. 77.22 at 30 cents on each $100 of value. It is paid at recording. Under Wis. Stat. 77.24 the county keeps 20 percent and the state takes the balance. Section 77.25 spells out the exemptions: transfers by will, descent or survivorship, some parent-to-child transfers for nominal consideration, and foreclosure deeds to a mortgage holder.

The deed goes to the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, in Milwaukee. Recording costs $30 a document, and every conveyance must include the electronic transfer return receipt. Bring cash, a check or a money order, because credit and debit cards are not taken.

Expect recording in three to five business days, handled in the order filings arrive, with the original returned by mail in one to two weeks. Trouble with the electronic return? The Wisconsin Department of Revenue answers at (608) 266-1594. Staff at the register's office will not draft documents or give legal advice, so most sellers hire a title company or an attorney. Questions about a pending recording go to (414) 278-4005.

sections.h2: Property taxes and back taxes in West Allis
sections.html:
West Allis taxes are billed by the city. Contact the City Treasurer for the due dates and any installment plan, and the City Assessor for your assessed value and property record, before you list. Wisconsin assessors aim for the full value a property would bring in a private sale, and the title company works out the split of the current-year bill when you close.

Delinquent taxes for 2024 and earlier years are handled by the Milwaukee County Treasurer, who covers every municipality in the county except the City of Milwaukee, so West Allis is included. State law attaches a delinquency charge of 18 percent a year, which makes early payment worthwhile. A call to (414) 278-4033 starts a payment plan. Paying online adds either a 2.55 percent card fee or a $1.50 e-check fee, collected by the processor.

With back taxes owing, get the Treasurer's payoff figure before you say yes to an offer, so the net you compare is real. The title company can pay that balance from your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a West Allis owner?
sections.html:
Ask every buyer for written terms and compare the options side by side.

  • Agent listing. Fits a house in presentable condition when you are not rushed.
  • For sale by owner. Keeps more of the price in your pocket but leaves disclosures and negotiations to you.
  • Cash buyer. Fits houses that need repairs, inherited or tenant-occupied properties, and owners trying to avoid foreclosure. Compare the net figure after title and recording costs.

Gather what a West Allis buyer will ask for before you list. The deed that put you on title, your latest mortgage statement, the most recent tax bill and any record of repairs belong in one folder. The assessor's property record is worth printing, since it shows your assessed value and the details the city holds on the house.

If the house came to you through an estate, add the papers showing who has authority to sign. If foreclosure worries you, talk to a title company early, because a sale can still close if the numbers work, and a cash offer can move on a date you choose.

When you accept an offer, the report clock starts, so complete the form right away. The title company runs the record search and prepares the deed and the electronic transfer return. At closing you sign the deed, pay the transfer fee, and clear any mortgage or tax balance from the proceeds. The deed is then recorded at the register's office. A cash sale follows these same steps without a lender's appraisal, so the date depends mostly on title work and recording.

faqs.q: How quickly can a West Allis house sell?
faqs.a: It turns on the buyer. A purchaser who needs no loan has no approval or appraisal to wait for, so the date comes down to title work and recording. A financed purchase adds showings, inspections and underwriting.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: The fee is $30 for each document, with the transfer fee from your electronic return receipt added. Payment is by cash, check or money order, since the office does not take cards.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property taxes in West Allis?
faqs.a: The Milwaukee County Treasurer, for 2024 and earlier years, in every county municipality except the City of Milwaukee. The delinquency charge set by state law is 18 percent a year. Call (414) 278-4033 about a payment plan.

faqs.q: Do I need a condition report if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Not when you are a personal representative or trustee who never lived there, because Chapter 709 excuses those fiduciaries. A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is also exempt from the transfer fee under s. 77.25.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee on a West Allis sale?
faqs.a: The grantor. It is 30 cents for each $100 of value, paid when the deed is recorded, and the electronic return goes to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue.
